title: 5.11.8 Check: Defender with classes
description: Seven multiple-choice questions on where things live after the refactor: hp on the enemy, a hit loop with no splices, what filter does not do, a parameter that is another object, static, the checklist, and the cost of a new fact. Checked instantly.

questions.question: After 5.11.4, where does an enemy's hp live?
options: In `enemyHp`, at the enemy's index
On its own Enemy object, as `this.hp`
In the sprite's text, which `takeHit()` reads back as a number
In `Enemy.spawned`
questions.explanation: Each Enemy keeps its own hp on `this`. The parallel array `enemyHp` is gone, and the sprite's text only shows the number.

questions.question: Why does `hitEnemies()` no longer splice anything?
options: `splice` is not allowed on an array of objects, only on numbers and sprites
A `for...of` loop has no index to splice with, so the finished objects stay in both arrays until the next round starts
Objects only change their state there; `clearFinished()` removes the finished ones once, at the end of the frame
Bullets can never hit twice, because `hits()` deletes the shot's sprite the moment it overlaps
questions.explanation: A hit calls `spend()` and `takeHit(1)`, and nothing leaves a list until `clearFinished()` runs at the end of the frame: finished in one place.

questions.question: What does `enemies = enemies.filter((e) => e.isAlive());` NOT do by itself?
options: Keep the enemies that are still alive in the list
Delete the finished enemies' sprites
Make a new array
Call `isAlive()` on each enemy
questions.explanation: `filter` only builds a new list. The finished enemies' sprites stay on screen unless something calls `remove()` on them first, which is why the remove loop runs before it.

questions.question: In `b.hits(e)`, what is `e`?
options: A number: the index of the enemy in `enemies`
The bullet's own sprite, which `hits()` compares with the enemy
The Enemy class itself, so `hits()` can test every enemy at once
Another object, an Enemy, handed to the bullet's method
questions.explanation: The parameter is another object, as in 5.8.12's `hit(other)`. Inside `hits(enemy)` the bullet reads `enemy.sprite` and asks `enemy.isAlive()`.

questions.question: Why is `spawned` declared `static`?
options: It is a fact about all enemies, so it belongs to the class (`Enemy.spawned`), not to one enemy
So it can never change once the first enemy has been built
So each enemy keeps its own count of how many enemies were built before it
Because a number kept on a class must be `static`, or the constructor will not run
questions.explanation: One counter for every enemy built lives on the class. Each new enemy adds 1 to it in the constructor, and `startRound()` sets it back to 0.

questions.question: Which class answers "no" to the checklist's first question, "more than one of this thing?"
options: Enemy
Bullet
Spawner
None of them
questions.explanation: There is only one spawner. It is a class anyway because its wave and pause change together, so a restart is one line, `spawner = new Spawner();`, that cannot forget a piece.

questions.question: Each enemy needs a shield value. In Part C, where does the change go?
options: In the Enemy constructor, and the one place that uses it
A new array, a push, two splices and a line in `startRound`
In every loop in `draw()`
Only in `Spawner`
questions.explanation: The enemy keeps its own facts, so a new fact is one more `this.shield` in the constructor plus the code that uses it. In Part B the same change needed a new array, a push, a splice in both removal copies and a line in `startRound`.
